nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, used to calibrate the SUMO simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The Data Availability statement indicates that the dataset is available from the corresponding author upon request, but no public link or DOI is provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time as functions of frame iterations during DRL training.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methods and hyperparams stated; training metrics cohere; but simulation road network configs and specific empirical training sets are closed (on request only) and code is not open.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Area plots of the median, Q1, and Q3 ranges of travel times for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL methods across time of day.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Sim setup given but relies on closed network setup/inputs. Valid visualization of stated simulations.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments. It is found that the performance of the PI-ALINEA method is not always better
nodes_sink.description: Comparisons of mean travel times (in seconds) between no controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL across 20 randomized simulation iterations.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Evaluations rely on a SUMO sim driven by unpublished proprietary road networks. Claim strictly coheres with table values.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline. The results further demonstrate the efficiency
nodes_sink.description: Heatmap-style temporal-spatial contour maps showing variations in vehicle speed across distances on the mainline from 8:00 to 9:00 for the three metering scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Displays extracted spatiotemporal simulated metrics. Tied to closed dataset constraint.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Timeline displaying interquartile ranges and median of on-ramp queue lengths.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methods partially transparent, results logic clearly compares derived downstream measures; lacks replicable public code/data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time)
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot correlating queue length and the proportion of red light time comparing PI-ALINEA and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Relationships derived effectively from described experiments, despite data-on-request limitation.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Dual line plots linking queue lengths to merging area downstream occupancy percentages across evaluation times.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Valid illustration using explicitly outlined simulator components, blocked upstream by data sharing policy.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots depicting statistical bounds of simulated traffic volumes binned in five minute intervals.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear statistical translation from sim; limited only by sim reproducibility limits upstream.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data
nodes_sink.description: Box-and-whisker sets describing travel time shifts occurring from specific informational inputs progressively perturbing varying input subsets across 20 repetitions.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: The perturbation process (which video features removed) requires assuming implementation nuances inside their sim configuration not entirely released.
